quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim MacMahon's first time in the chapel room
quotes.excerpt: I'm actually in the chapel room. I got to tell you, this is a first for me.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: How did you find it? How did you even know where to go?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I'm actually in the chapel room. I got to tell you, this is a first for me, but here I am.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers spoil ring night at Madison Square Garden
quotes.excerpt: It was a quality win for the Sixers because they got a victory on the road.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The Philadelphia 76ers go into Madison Square Garden, ruin ring night with a victory over the Knicks. It was not a particularly well-played game, but it was a quality win for the Sixers because they got a victory on the road in an emotional environment when LeBron James and Joel Embiid both didn't give them much offensively.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I'm going to dispute the last part. They didn't score a lot. I thought that they both moved the ball well, passed the ball well. I thought Embiid made a lot of good decisions.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's undefeated streak since being traded
quotes.excerpt: My analysis is Jaylen Brown's undefeated since being traded and the Celtics are winless.
quotes.quote: My analysis is Jaylen Brown's undefeated since being traded and the Celtics are winless. So take that for what it's worth.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James playing defensive center for the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: LeBron James played dozens of possessions at defensive center.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: LeBron James played dozens of possessions at defensive center. You knew the 76ers were thin at center. Adem Bona is just coming back from injury and Ariel Hukporti is lost for the year, so their backups behind Joel Embiid are really weak. They put LeBron at center for many possessions when Embiid was on the court. A core strategy in this game was they put Embiid onto Josh Hart, kind of hid him if you will, and then had LeBron defending Carl-Anthony Towns.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: How about the biggest defensive play of the game being late in the game? He gets to the top of the square to get a piece of Mikal Bridges' layup attempt and just get a huge block. I thought it was the biggest stop of the game.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Adam Silver's decision to have team members present rings
quotes.excerpt: They didn't have Adam Silver give out the rings. They had members and the descendants.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: They didn't have Adam Silver give out the rings. They had members and the descendants of the 73 title team give out the rings, which was cool and different. But you know how Adam Silver and James Dolan have a frosty relationship.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Hey though, the NBA Cup ribbon is hanging now from the rafters though. I mean, is that a little bit of an olive branch? I don't know.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl-Anthony Towns' performance in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: Carl-Anthony Towns averaged almost eight assists a game. He was thriving in that point center role.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: When these two teams played in the playoffs last year, which was a sweep, Carl-Anthony Towns averaged almost eight assists a game. He was thriving in that point center, well not really point center, but sort of the offensive hub role.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Towns will pick up dumb offensive fouls and he looked like a rocket kicking his leg up and getting fouled there.

quotes.speaker: Mat Ishbia
quotes.summary_phrase: How the Suns organization makes big decisions
quotes.excerpt: It's a collaboration. I'm extremely engaged from every detail, every question.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: When you come to a big decision, what is the process you go through to make a decision like that? Whether it's to make a big trade, to make a hire, to make a firing? As the head of the organization, how do you get there?

text_blocks.speaker: Mat Ishbia
text_blocks.text: It's a collaboration. I'm extremely engaged from every detail, every question. We've got alignment from me to the CEO Josh Bartelstein, to the GM Brian Gregory, to the coach Mike Budenholzer, and then down to our players as well. But the four of us sit in a room and talk and debate everything. On the playing time and rotations, coach Bud is the final decision maker. On who we draft, Brian Gregory is the final decision maker. Everyone has their role, but everyone's thoughts are put into it.

quotes.speaker: Mat Ishbia
quotes.summary_phrase: Mat Ishbia on being an engaged owner
quotes.excerpt: I'm extremely engaged from every detail, every question. If people don't like that, then they're not going to be Suns fans.
quotes.quote: I'm extremely engaged from every detail, every question. We just signed a new two-way player and I was involved with that. Every detail of the team, I'm involved with. And if people don't like that, then they're not going to be Phoenix Suns and Phoenix Mercury fans. If they do like that, we'll see how the results come out. But we're going to do our best and we're completely aligned.

quotes.speaker: Mat Ishbia
quotes.summary_phrase: Mat Ishbia's business relationship with his brother Justin
quotes.excerpt: He's my big brother. He's my minority partner in the Mercury and the Suns.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: How do you operate with your brother? Your brother Justin, very successful businessman of his own right. He is a partner of yours. Do you work together that much? Are you going to consult with him on White Sox deals?

text_blocks.speaker: Mat Ishbia
text_blocks.text: We're best friends. He's my big brother. He's my minority partner in the Mercury and the Suns. He owns about 18-19%. And I'm the same thing. I own, you know, between me and him we own about 45% of the White Sox and he'll be the main guy in the White Sox and I'll be the minority. And so we're excited about that. That's still 5-8 years away. But we're extremely engaged with everything.

quotes.speaker: Mat Ishbia
quotes.summary_phrase: Mat Ishbia's support for NBA expansion
quotes.excerpt: I'm supportive of growing the game, so I'm pro expansion.
quotes.quote: I'm supportive of growing the game, so I'm pro expansion. Obviously, it depends on the situation and making sure there's the right partners and the right value. But I believe that Vegas is a market that we need to fill. I think Seattle is one. I know there's been talk about Mexico City. The way I look at it is expanding the game. NBA is a global game, and having 30 is a limited number. Can you get to 32? I'm going to go that many more. Can you grow, can you cover a big market like Vegas? I don't care that it's close to Phoenix. I'm excited. I think there's abundance, there's opportunity everywhere, and I'm supportive of it.

quotes.speaker: Mat Ishbia
quotes.summary_phrase: Mat Ishbia on the Suns' long-term roster strategy
quotes.excerpt: We want to put a long runway as we have an ascending younger team.
quotes.quote: Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale, we loved having them. But as we're trying to build this thing and we want to put a long runway as we have an ascending younger team. Miles Bridges is exactly what we're looking for. A tough, rugged player, physical, athletic. He's a great teammate. And so he was a target of ours for more than a year or two. We were looking, how do we get a guy like Miles Bridges? And we were able to get him, put him next to Dylan Brooks in the front line. And then obviously we got Devin and Jaylen in the backcourt. We feel really good about that along with the rest of our team. And so we're really happy with it. We're excited for this season and Miles will be a great part of our organization going forward.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Chet Holmgren's defensive impact against Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: Chet Holmgren was the primary defender on Victor Wembanyama, who had an absolutely miserable offensive performance.
quotes.quote: Chet Holmgren came out and was aggressive and he came out and was the primary defender on Victor Wembanyama, who had an absolutely miserable offensive performance. And look, did Wembanyama miss some shots that were decent looks for him? Yes, but he never got anything resembling a rhythm on the offensive end.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Williams as a secondary creator
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Williams is an outstanding second guy in against historically dominant big men.
quotes.quote: Jalen Williams is an outstanding second guy in against historically dominant big men. Remember the Lou Dort Joker fracas last year and then Jalen Williams is in there and there's that frame of Joker getting the crazy eyes looking right at Jalen Williams.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Williams is an extraordinarily gifted offensive player, but still pretty raw, still developing.
quotes.quote: Jalen Williams is an extraordinarily gifted offensive player, but still pretty raw, still developing, and there's some real inconsistency there. And at this point, he does not yet have a go-to move.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.excerpt: Unfortunately, it's the lob dunk. It's either the three-pointer which nobody can defend but everybody wants him to take.
quotes.quote: Unfortunately, it's the lob dunk. It's either the three-pointer which nobody can defend but everybody wants him to take. And the move that he has that is not really stopping needs another player.
